subgroups.test: exact two-sided sign test on the calls only one of the two got right, per kind of call
subgroups.adjustment_words: Each kind of call carries three p-values: before any adjustment; adjusted (Bonferroni) for the 3 kinds of call tested, the correction the adopted method applies across kinds of call; and adjusted for all 9 subgroup comparisons served for this sample (the 3 kinds and the 6 per-coach comparisons).

kinds.sentence: Number calls: 41 of the 73 counted forecasts. On the 40 the simple prediction could also be scored on, the coaches were right 26 times and the simple prediction that nothing would change 23 times. Tested on the 5 where only one of the two was right (the coaches alone 4, the simple prediction alone 1), an exact two-sided sign test gives p = 0.38 before any adjustment; p = 1.00 adjusted for the 3 kinds of call tested, and p = 1.00 counting all 9 subgroup comparisons (Bonferroni): no detectable difference.

kinds.label: baseline_better
kinds.sentence: Direction calls: 21 of the 73 counted forecasts. On them, the coaches were right 4 times and the simple prediction that nothing would change 16 times. Tested on the 20 where only one of the two was right (the coaches alone 4, the simple prediction alone 16), an exact two-sided sign test gives p = 0.012 before any adjustment; p = 0.035 adjusted for the 3 kinds of call tested, and p = 0.11 counting all 9 subgroup comparisons (Bonferroni): the simple prediction was right more often in this group, and that holds after adjusting for the 3 kinds of call tested, but not once all 9 subgroup comparisons are counted.

Sealed day-one predictions: 11 of the 73 counted forecasts. On them, the coaches were right 7 times and the simple prediction that nothing would change once. Tested on the 8 where only one of the two was right (the coaches alone 7, the simple prediction alone 1), an exact two-sided sign test gives p = 0.070 before any adjustment; p = 0.21 adjusted for the 3 kinds of call tested, and p = 0.63 counting all 9 subgroup comparisons (Bonferroni): no detectable difference.

subgroups.caveat: Exploratory, not a headline result: these comparisons split the same calls by kind, after the fact, and were not the question the sample was gathered to answer. A low p-value in one kind of call does not show that the simple prediction is the better forecaster: the groups are small, several comparisons were tested, and calls that share a measure and a window are not independent, so every p-value here is optimistic.

archive.label: As first graded, before the eligibility and verification rules were corrected

verification_summary.why_changed: The record changed because the rules for which calls count, and for re-checking each grade, were corrected — not because the coaches improved. As first graded, the coaches were right on 89 of 208 calls (43%). Under the current rules 73 of the 208 graded calls qualify, and every call left out is listed with the reason.
verification_summary.rules: Counted: a public call graded right or wrong whose latest verification record reproduced its grade (or the recorded correction of it) and whose approved classification keeps it as a checkable forecast, counted once per forecast. The simple prediction that nothing would change is scored on exactly the same calls; a call it could not be scored on counts as its miss. Intervals are 95% Wilson intervals; the comparison is an exact two-sided sign test on the calls only one of the two got right. Calls that share a metric and a window are not independent, so both are optimistic.

method_history.note: One label per forecaster from a fixed ±0.15 mean-gap trip and a Brier-skill gate; retired because it answered three different questions with one threshold.

Three separate questions — estimability across confidence levels, over/under-confidence at an observed level (exact test, Holm-corrected), and skill against the same-call baseline — each with its own interval; adopted by the owner on 2026-11-09.

estimability.method: Levels are the 10 stated-confidence bands, each with an exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval. Across levels is estimable with at least 2 levels of at least 17 calls (exact interval no wider than 0.5) and at least 20 calls of the rarer outcome (10 per parameter); the estimate is the logistic recalibration slope with a Wald 95% interval.

confidence_direction.method: Exact two-sided binomial test of each level's hits against its mean stated confidence (conservative when the stated values inside a level differ), Holm-adjusted across the levels tested, family-wise alpha 0.05. Calls that share a metric and a window are not independent, so the p-values are optimistic.

method.note: Public totals, denominators and accuracy count only publication-eligible calls: a call is eligible when what it is about and what it is graded on are publishable sources. A call about the private journal (whether, when or what he writes), or about mood, felt sense or another private self-report, or graded on one, is kept in full privately with its grading history and is left out of every public list and number. The calls left out are not counted anywhere on this site.

disclosure: Self-graded: every prediction here was resolved against the platform's own data by a deterministic evaluator — no human scoring. Brier score: 0 is perfect, 0.25 is the always-say-50% baseline, lower is better. The calibration verdict is calibration-v2 (`assessment_v2`, adopted 2026-11-09): three separate questions, each with its own test and interval — can calibration across confidence levels be estimated; is there statistically supported over- or under-confidence at an observed confidence level (exact binomial test, Holm-corrected); does a coach beat the same-call guess that nothing changes. Failing to detect a problem is never proof of good calibration. The older `calibration` / `label` / `score` fields are deprecated (see `calibration_method`). The platform-wide card scores skill against a STRATIFIED base rate — coach calls, hypothesis bets and each forecasting MODEL's interval forecasts separately, every one against its own climatology (the daily metric engine and the weekly training prescription are different models and are never counted as one number) — so pooling strata with different base rates cannot manufacture a skill no stratum has, and each stratum's own n, Brier and skill are served beside it; calibration-v2 assesses each stratum separately and never pools them. Voided bets: a reset voids — never grades — every still-open pre-registered bet; each is recorded in the ledger and counted in `voided` so the graded denominator is honest. They are excluded from Brier because they never resolved. Every hit rate here carries its 95% Wilson interval (`accuracy_ci95`) alongside `n` — a hit rate off a small n reads as more precise than it is.
